answer.read: Ravensteiner is capacity-constrained and allocating: order intake is very strong (doc:20260327-M2), it allocates by last year's call-offs (news:20260822), and it cannot confirm our full forecast for part:340010 while prioritising firm long-term commitments (doc:20260918-P10). What it needs is commitment, and we already give it full volume and a 36-month term at its own 56 d lead time. It moved from €32.20 to €31.70 and accepted our should-cost data (verified). That still leaves a wide margin over its estimated full cost of about €24.31. Price changes above two percent go through a pricing committee (doc:20260310-M1), so it will concede in steps. Its financials are stable (credit index 159 unchanged), so the relationship charge has no special pressure behind it.
answer.message: Thank you for your revised proposal and for confirming the should-cost data. We are offering exactly the firm long-term commitment you said you prioritise: our full annual volume over a thirty-six-month term, on your stated lead time. With that security for your capacity planning, we expect a price much closer to our established price level, and our attached term sheet reflects this.
answer.reason: E0 is the only selectable option, since every alternative term mix has an unknown trade value for the supplier. It keeps our cost well below the standing offer:70410-1. The supplier is still open and conceding at a steady pace, so accepting now would leave value on the table. Citing our recent order prices is a new argument kind the supplier has not heard yet, and it anchors the gap to today's price.
